title: Lum and Abner
paragraphs: A long-running rural comedy centered on Lum Edwards and Abner Peabody, proprietors of the Jot 'Em Down Store in the fictional community of Pine Ridge, Arkansas.

Long-running rural comedy created and performed by Chester Lauck and Norris Goff. Most of the run used a short serialized strip centered on the Jot Em Down Store in Pine Ridge, with a documented 1948-1950 half-hour comedy-variety detour before returning to short-form episodes.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Mutual serial era (April 2, 1934 to August 30, 1935) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Blue Network serial era (September 2, 1935 to February 25, 1938) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], CBS serial era (February 28, 1938 to March 29, 1940) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and NBC Pacific serial era (May 26, 1941 to September 19, 1941) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|chester-lauck|Chester Lauck]] (performer), [[person|norris-goff|Norris Goff]] (performer), Lou Crosby (announcer and performer), Carlton Brickert (announcer), Clarence Hartzell (performer), Gene Baker (announcer), and Barbara Stanwyck (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and [[org|org.06124d0208d8bc7b|KARK]].
The stories often return to General store and small business, World War II home front, School and education, Movies and show business, Local politics and civic office, and Wartime rationing.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Waters, Arkansas renamed Pine Ridge in honor of Lum and Abner, Lum and Abner during the World War II home front, and Lum and Abner during radio format and television-era change.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]], [[show|the-phil-harris-alice-faye-show|The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], and [[show|the-great-gildersleeve|The Great Gildersleeve]].
